_comment: Default knobs for workload/. A scenario config (e.g. agentx_glm52.json) layers on top of this, and command-line --set layers on top of that. Every path is either absolute or resolved relative to the GEAK repository root.

target._comment: What this run optimizes. A scenario config MUST fill in `model`: scripts/target.py refuses to start a run whose config filename or run_root does not carry a recognisable token of it, and cross-checks `image`/`commits` against what the stages observed and recorded. This exists because a run once carried a planning-phase label (`agentx_dsv4`) for a GLM-5.2 stack from end to end -- every number was right and every label was wrong. `name_tokens` whitelists a deliberate abbreviation the tokeniser cannot derive (e.g. "dsv4" for DeepSeek-V4). Set `enforce` to false only with a written reason.

params.selection: Broader candidate discovery through the profile slot; plan complete operators up to the task limit and retain every deferred candidate with its reason.
params._note_selection: Top 10 and overall >0.5% are heuristic discovery cutoffs requested to explore beyond Muse's former three UTs, not calibrated performance thresholds. The unchanged skill selector takes these explicit arguments; kernel KEEP and E2E bands are unchanged.

params._note_task_limit: Capacity policy requested for an eight-GPU campaign, not a performance threshold: plan at most eight independent optimization tasks in profile, then optimize every delivered task. A whole-node collective still needs its real GPU group. Over-limit deliveries must be replanned, never silently truncated by max_tasks or exclusions.

report._comment: Periodic reporting, on by default: `stage.py all` starts scripts/watch.py, which every interval_sec appends a block to <run_root>/PROGRESS.md, rewrites progress.json, and re-renders <run_root>/REPORT.md from whatever the stages have finished. A run that reports only at the end is one nobody can act on, and a run killed before its last stage would otherwise leave no report at all. Turn it off with `stage.py all --no-report` or enabled:false. interval_sec is 1800 because the stages that take hours write something every few minutes, so a half-hourly block is one screen of real movement rather than a log. --- on_stall is separate and defaults to "report": the monitor describes what it sees and acts on nothing. Setting it to "restart-attempt" lets it kill one specific, provable condition -- a live stage that has written nothing under $OUT for stall_sec AND whose process tree used less than min_cpu_sec of CPU over that window. One signal alone lies (the long stages legitimately spend forty minutes building an image or loading 892 GB of weights without touching $OUT), so both are required; stall_sec 5400 is chosen well clear of that longest observed legitimate silence. Killing the attempt is how it resumes -- the dispatcher's next attempt opens with a continuation prompt listing the artifacts already on disk -- and nothing is deleted. After max_interventions on one stage it stops acting and says so, because a stage that wedges that often needs a person. The old key name "watch" is still read if present.

runner_env._comment: state_dir_base must sit on local disk, never on NFS (the agent's sqlite gets poisoned there). env_file points at a credential/gateway file kept **outside the repo**; see runners/claude.env.example for the template — keys are never committed. Leaving model null uses the CLI's own default rather than inheriting an ANTHROPIC_MODEL that may already be exported in the environment.
